subject: Post-call: POC plan recap + request to add refund-extraction use case
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + POC success criteria (draft)

Hi Carlos — great chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the trial: 

Summary of what we heard
- Goals: Faster, more accurate post-purchase routing and insights for returns/refunds; reduce manual triage.
- Primary success criteria (proposed):
  - Intent classification accuracy >= 95% on annotated test set
  - Extraction precision >= 90% (for reasons/entities defined in sample schema)
  - End-to-end 99th percentile latency < 300ms for single-turn inference
  - Ingest and index 50k historical tickets for offline evaluation
- Timeline: 6-week trial (data ingest + integration week, model tuning + eval weeks, final acceptance)
- Owners: BrightCommerce: Carlos (project lead), Redwood: Monica (CS), Ben (integration), Sean (AM).

Attachments: [Attachment: trial_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 48 KB)]

Next steps
1) Please confirm owners and the dates below for a planned start week of Oct 18.
2) If the success criteria above miss anything you need (e.g., throughput/burst testing), flag it now so we can bake it into the plan.
3) Monica will share onboarding checklist and data template once you confirm start.

Thanks again — I’ll hold off provisioning test capacity until we get a thumbs-up from you.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128
Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@brightcommerce.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCommerce - Data & ML team <ml@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + POC success criteria (draft)

Thanks Sean — nice summary. A few adjustments from our side that are important before we lock the plan: 

1) Add use case: We want to add "refund reason extraction" as a second, high-priority use case to validate alongside routing. That's a structured-extraction task with slightly different evaluation needs.
2) Criteria nuance: For extraction, we care about both precision and recall — target precision >= 92% and recall >= 85% on our annotated sample. For routing intents, still aiming for >=95% accuracy.
3) Throughput: Can we include a short burst test (500 concurrent lightweight requests) to measure tail latency and per-GPU throughput? This matters for our peak-day traffic planning.
4) Timeline: If possible, could we compress the trial by one week? We have a board review on Nov 5 and would prefer results earlier. If that requires reducing scope, we can prioritize refund extraction + top 6 intents instead of full 50k ingest.

Attached is our priority list with a sketch of which flows are must-have vs nice-to-have.

Attachments: [Attachment: BrightCommerce-Priority-List.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12 KB)]

Can you confirm whether adding the extraction use case mid-trial is feasible and what trade-offs you recommend?

Cheers,
Carlos Vega
Head of Product Operations, BrightCommerce
c.vega@brightcommerce.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap + POC success criteria (draft) — request to rebaseline mid-trial

Folks — forwarding Carlos' asks. TL;DR: customer wants to add a new "refund reason extraction" use case, tighten extraction precision/recall targets, add a burst throughput check, and potentially compress timeline by one week (they are OK reducing scope). Need quick ops/engineering input so we can respond today.

My quick read / suggested rebaseline:
- Keep overall trial at 5 weeks (compress by 1). Drop full 50k ingest to a 20k sampling of high-priority tickets and a focused annotated set for extraction.
- Acceptance matrix: add extraction targets (P >= 92%, R >= 85%) and maintain intent accuracy >= 95% on top 6 intents.
- Add a 2-hour burst window in week 3 to run the 500-concurrent request profile (we can schedule on dedicated capacity). Rishi, can you confirm whether quantized models we recommended will hold up for the burst or if we need a fallback model?
- Ben, need estimate for integration effort to deliver the annotated sample ingestion + webhook for the burst test.
- Monica, can you update the trial_plan_v1 -> v2 with new milestones and owners and send to Carlos for approval?

Proposed reply to customer once we confirm feasibility (I can send): summary of new acceptance criteria, a 5-week compressed timeline, and confirmation of owners + a shared Drive link to revised plan.

Attachments: [Attachment: rebaseline_matrix_v1.csv (text/csv, 3 KB)]

Thanks — Sean

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@brightcommerce.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Updated trial plan and rebaseline proposal (trial_plan_v2)

Hi Carlos — thanks for the fast feedback and the priority list. We discussed internally and put together a condensed v2 plan that folds in the refund-extraction use case and the burst test while compressing the timeline as requested. High level: 

- Updated timeline: 5 weeks total (start week Oct 25)
  - Week 0: Data sampling & annotation kickoff (20k sample + 2k annotated extraction set)
  - Week 1: Integration & baseline model run
  - Week 2: Model tuning for extraction & intent mapping
  - Week 3: Burst throughput window + evaluation runs
  - Week 4: Acceptance review & handoff to BrightCommerce engineers

- Acceptance matrix (shortened):
  - Intent accuracy (top 6 intents) >= 95% on sample test set
  - Extraction precision >= 92% and recall >= 85% on annotated set
  - 99th percentile latency < 350ms under normal load; burst test results documented (no hard SLA during burst, but we’ll provide throughput guidance)
  - Integration endpoints operational and sample ingest validated

Owners: 
- BrightCommerce: Carlos (eng lead), Priya (data lead) [cc not included in thread due to inbox restriction].
- Redwood: Monica (CS owner, week-to-week coordinator), Ben (integration lead), Rishi (inference reliability).

We attached the updated plan: trial_plan_v2.pdf and included a rebaseline matrix mapping each original acceptance item to the new condensed criteria. If that looks good, please reply "Approved" and we’ll finalize schedule and provision a dedicated slot for the burst test (suggested window: Nov 2, 09:00–11:00 PT).

Attachments: [Attachment: trial_plan_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 62 KB)]

Quick note on trade-offs: compressing to 5 weeks and reducing the ingest set means we will surface high-confidence issues faster but may miss some long-tail intents. We recommend a follow-on expansion after acceptance to cover the full 50k history. Happy to discuss trade-offs on the call if you’d like.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference
